STRIX_FINDINGS_TRIAGE.name: Rate-limit bypass in /api/audit via client-controlled forwarded IP headers
STRIX_FINDINGS_TRIAGE.root_cause: requestIdentity() in lib/request-rate-limit.mjs trusted client-supplied x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip, allowing an attacker to rotate the header per request to mint fresh rate-limit buckets and bypass the durable Supabase-backed rate limiter on /api/audit.
STRIX_FINDINGS_TRIAGE.remediation: requestIdentity() now consults only the trusted platform client-IP header (x-nf-client-connection-ip on Netlify, with client-ip as a secondary). When the platform supplies no client IP, the function returns the sentinel 'unknown' so all such requests share one bucket. Added regression tests in lib/request-rate-limit.test.mjs proving spoofed x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip / cf-connecting-ip values do not mint new buckets. Updated app/api/chat/route.test.js to use the trusted header. 218/218 tests pass.

STRIX_FINDINGS_TRIAGE.name: Rate-Limit Bypass in /api/chat via Client-Supplied Forwarding Headers
STRIX_FINDINGS_TRIAGE.root_cause: Same root cause as CWE-770: requestIdentity() trusted attacker-controlled forwarding headers on the public /api/chat endpoint, allowing an attacker to drain the MiniMax budget by rotating x-forwarded-for per request.
STRIX_FINDINGS_TRIAGE.remediation: Same fix as CWE-770: requestIdentity() now uses only the trusted platform client-IP header. Verified the test suite covers both bypass vectors.
